haiku-low.q1: They do not differ: both return HTTP 401 and the login page with "Invalid email or password". Unknown emails still run a bcrypt check against a dummy hash, so timing is the same.
haiku-low.q2: The lock check runs first, so the server returns HTTP 429 without checking the password, even if the password is correct. The lock lasts 15 minutes.
haiku-low.q3: If the browser's cookie pointed to a session, that session row is deleted. A brand-new session ID is then created for the browser.
haiku-low.q4: Only a long random session ID (sid), with no user data. The cookie is flagged HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax. The document does not say more about script access.
haiku-low.q5: 12 hours after login, regardless of activity. The 30-minute idle timeout does not extend it, so the session ends at the absolute limit.
haiku-low.q6: It clears the cookie and redirects the browser to /login. No protected content is shown.
haiku-low.q7: The session row is deleted before the reply is sent. With no cookie or an unknown ID, it still clears the cookie and redirects to /login.
haiku-low.q8: Session state is kept in the Postgres sessions table. Any instance looks up the sid there, so no in-process memory or sticky sessions are used.
haiku-low.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table, one row per failed attempt. Failures count only if failed_at is within the last 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: It checks the row exists and that neither timeout has passed: now minus last_seen_at is at most 30 minutes, and now minus created_at is at most 12 hours. If valid, it writes last_seen_at = now.
haiku-low.q11: HTTP 503 with a plain "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable, please try again" page. No session is created.
haiku-low.q12: A cleanup job on each instance, running every 10 minutes, deletes expired sessions, old login_failures and past login_locks. It only saves space; expiry is enforced on read.

sonnet.q1: They don't differ. Both get HTTP 401 and the login page showing "Invalid email or password". For an unknown email the app still runs a bcrypt check against a dummy hash so timing doesn't reveal it.
sonnet.q2: The email is locked out, so it gets HTTP 429 and no password check is done, even if the password is correct. The lock check comes before the password check.
sonnet.q3: The old session row is deleted and a brand-new session ID is always created, with a Set-Cookie for the new sid.
sonnet.q4: Only the random session ID (sid), with no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It is also Secure and SameSite=Lax.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login (the absolute timeout), regardless of activity. Continuous use keeps the idle timeout from firing, but the absolute timeout still ends the session.
sonnet.q6: It clears the cookie and redirects to /login.
sonnet.q7: The session row is deleted before the reply is sent. If the session is already gone (no cookie or unknown ID), the delete is a no-op and it behaves the same: clear the cookie and redirect to /login.
sonnet.q8: In Postgres, in the sessions table. Both instances share that database, so either one looks up the sid from the cookie in Postgres on each request. No process memory or sticky sessions are used.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table, one row (email, failed_at) per failed attempt. The server counts rows for that email with failed_at newer than 10 minutes.
sonnet.q10: It compares now against last_seen_at (more than 30 min is expired) and against created_at (more than 12 h is expired). When valid, it writes last_seen_at = now.
sonnet.q11: HTTP 503 with a plain "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable, please try again" page. No session is created and no one is let in.
sonnet.q12: A cleanup job on each app instance, running every 10 minutes, deletes expired sessions rows. Expiry is also enforced on every read, so cleanup only saves space.
